transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I’m losing a lot of time checking things, basically. I’ll re-read emails and texts over and over, reopen folders I already looked at, and replay conversations in my head before I leave the house or start work. It’s like I’m trying to prove to myself I didn’t make some serious mistake, and it’s starting to get in the way.
Do you ever feel that your thoughts or behaviors are excessive, or do they take up a lot of your time each day?

Yes. I do think it’s excessive, and it definitely takes up a lot of time. I’ll get stuck re-reading an email or a text several times, or reopening the same folders even though I know I already checked them. Sometimes I’ll replay a conversation in my head before I leave or start working, just trying to convince myself I didn’t miss something or make a serious mistake. It can eat up chunks of the day.
Are these thoughts that keep coming back unwanted and feel intrusive, or are they more about just being overly careful about things you need to get done?

They feel unwanted and intrusive, not just careful. Like even when I’m trying to focus on a system design or getting ready for a lesson, a thought barges in that maybe I sent the wrong message to my ex-wife, or mishandled some family photos, or let someone in the community down. I’ll know I’ve already gone over it, but I can’t just let it pass.
When these intrusive thoughts come up, do you feel driven to perform certain behaviors or mental acts to reduce the anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Yes, I do. When the thought comes up, I feel like I have to check something to calm down. I’ll re-read the same email or text, reopen folders I already looked through, or go over a conversation in my head again and again before I leave the house or start work. It’s like I’m trying to prove to myself I didn’t make some big mistake, even when part of me knows I already checked.
Do you ever feel like your concerns are irrational or unlikely, or do you worry they might be completely true and you just can't take the chance?

I’m not completely sure how to put it. In the moment, it feels like I can’t take the chance, even if part of me knows I may be overdoing it. I don’t always fully believe the worry, but I also don’t feel comfortable ignoring it.
Would you say the thoughts themselves bother you more, or the things you feel you have to do in response to them?

I think it’s more the things I feel like I have to do. The thoughts are upsetting, but what really gets in the way is losing all that time re-reading emails and texts, reopening folders, or replaying conversations in my head before I can leave the house or start work. It feels like I’m trying to prove to myself I didn’t make some serious mistake.
Have these thoughts or behaviors started to interfere with your work, relationships, or other important areas of your life?

Yes, it has. At work I’ve slowed down enough that I’ve missed some design milestones, which isn’t like me. I’ve also had to postpone mentoring sessions I used to handle pretty reliably.

And outside of work, there was a youth coding workshop that mattered to me, and I ended up late and not really prepared. I felt pretty embarrassed about that.
On average, do these thoughts and the things you feel you have to do in response to them take up more than an hour of your day?

Yes, definitely more than an hour most days. It comes in chunks, but between re-reading emails and texts, opening folders again to check them, and replaying conversations in my head before I leave or start work, it adds up pretty fast. It feels like I’m trying to convince myself I didn’t make some serious mistake.
